values: A MAL character lottery, team comparison tool and browser roguelike idle battler.
Anime/manga fans who want to turn their public MAL collection into a team and explore randomized battles.
Lottery, three MALchups comparisons, and the Jobber Journeys testing loop with stats, items, events, stages and bosses.
Import or demo → roll five → Depart → stage and pathways → choose fight/event → resolve → reward/replacement → continue.
Boss on upcoming floor 10,20,…; item choice at each 5 cleared floors; three lives; game over resets team and inventory.
MAL favorites determine rarity. Rarity sets the bounded random BST. Canonical power and VS Battles tiers never set base stats.
Current saves are server-side JSON linked to browser import IDs. No account sign-in, cross-device save or multiplayer is implemented.
12 Oct 2026. Baseline statuses reflect repository inspection and prior work; acceptance checks start Pending.
Use Tracker dropdowns. Set acceptance to Pass only after checking Specifications. Filter Origin to separate your plans from suggestions.
Reviewed complete becomes Checked only when status is Implemented/Done and acceptance check is Pass.
P1 = recommended next work; P2 = after the foundation; P3 = later exploration; Maintain = existing behavior. Priorities are editable.
Phases are sequencing suggestions. No dates, estimates, owners or delivery commitments have been invented.
Reliable mechanics, saves and balance measurements
Regression baseline, save recovery and event schema work
Valid encounter pools, tested bands and reviewed difficulty curve
More passives, items, events and stages
Every new effect has tests, feedback and balancing notes
Achievements, identity, growth and possible PvP
Approve design and persistence boundaries first
Reload/retry cannot reroll saved stats, duplicate items, remove a second life or change a selected encounter.
Boss passive effects are not active.
Players can inspect effects, targets, ability triggers and outcome rules. Support touch, keyboard and reduced motion.
Most cataloged passives are descriptions only.
Measure encounter duration, win rate, stage outliers and median floor reached with seeded teams. Treat 20–40 seconds as an initial target, not a measured guarantee.
Stable IDs and valid catalogs. Listed-only passives stay distinct from working effects. Bosses get mechanics only when implemented and tested.
Floor-based enemy scaling is not implemented.
Preparation may be slow for large lists. Rolls and battles use prepared data. Add caching, bounded retries and measured budgets before setting numeric service targets.
Achievements and signed-in saves are not implemented.
No real-money economy, canonical stat templates, element systems or level growth is required for the next progression release.
README and some UI notes lag behind the code.
SUG-01/02/04/08 and PLAN-10/23 first. Then one boss passive, one progression band and one richer event before expanding all content.

values: Match IDs to Tracker. Evidence refers to repository source inspected on 12 Oct 2026. Future criteria are proposed test targets.
Import public anime and manga lists from a username or profile URL. Offer an offline demo without a MAL client ID.
Public profile imports both media types. Private/unavailable lists explain the failure. Demo works without network access.
Collect characters for each imported title and deduplicate by MAL character ID.
A character in multiple titles appears once in the pool and retains its source titles.
Show import counts and progress. Cancel safely and retry incomplete titles while retaining fetched data.
Cancel stops further queued work. Resume retains existing characters and retries unfinished titles.
Draw 5–10 distinct characters from the prepared pool. Allow early draws where the current pool is sufficient.
No duplicate character within one draw. Early draws show limited-pool context. Later draws reuse saved data.
Filter eligible draws by an editable minimum MAL favorite count.
The threshold is a nonnegative integer. Unknown counts are excluded. Insufficient pools explain the limit.
Assign N/R/SR/SSR/UR from favorites. Display rarity labels, frames, high-rarity glows and rolling previews. Use the 225:350 portrait ratio.
Rarity boundaries match rarity.ts. Portraits retain the full image. Reduced-motion preference disables unnecessary animation.
Import two independently configured profiles. Both sides use one shared 5–10 draw size and mirrored desktop layouts.
Same profile can be used twice. Controls and results remain usable on desktop and stacked mobile layouts.
Draw both teams concurrently, finish mode-specific lookups, then show the winner and totals. Place the next draw button below the result.
All three modes run from one button. Failed or incomplete draws never reuse a stale winner. Controls lock during the operation.
Compare total MAL character favorites across equal-size teams.
Higher total wins. Equal totals draw. Unknown counts are visibly treated as zero.
Each character contributes its highest-scored anime/manga source within the imported collection. Compare team sums.
Completed imports and sufficient rated characters are required. Each character contributes exactly one community score.
Use the highest explicit VS Battles tier on the matched character page. Handle name order, variants and franchise context.
Missing matches remain unranked. Source links reveal the selected page. The highest ranked character determines the team result.
Roll five distinct pool characters. Guarantee one character with a cataloged ability when eligible characters exist.
Exactly five members. At least one cataloged passive. Ineligible pools show a helpful error. A listed passive need not yet have battle mechanics.
Generate bounded HP/ATK/DEF/SPD with exact rarity BST and retain values on each unit instance.
N/R/SR/SSR/UR totals are 500/520/545/570/600. Refresh preserves stats. Replacement creates a new instance with new stats.
Show series, favorites, rarity, passive descriptions, base stats and colored modifier bars.
HP/ATK/DEF/SPD/BST are readable. Gear and keyword bonuses are separated from stored base values. Tooltips work with keyboard focus.
Separate pathway selection, battle replay and inventory. FIGHT and CONTINUE switch views and scroll to the relevant section.
Players can follow a run without repeatedly scrolling past all earlier controls. Switching views retains the active run.
Offer three distinct five-character teams from the imported pool. Hide opponent favorites. Allow one replacement after a qualifying victory.
Selections are locked after choosing. A victory grants no more than one saved replacement. Empty slots can be refilled.
Show three life orbs. Loss removes one life. At zero lives, reset progress, inventory and team. Include a testing reset button.
Repeated result requests do not remove extra lives. Reset restores three lives and floor progress, removes inventory and creates a new team.
Speed determines ATB fill. Full ATB triggers a random living target attack and resets the gauge. Damage = 25 × 2ATK / (ATK + DEF).
Each unit has a battle-only gauge. Living enemies receive valid attacks. Damage, attack lines and hit feedback agree with the replay.
Compute and save battle outcomes on the server. Play elapsed-time-based replays in the client, including when returning from another tab.
Outcome cannot change with browser rendering speed. Returning to a backgrounded tab catches up. Reload restoration requires explicit QA.
Play battle clocks at 2× speed and accelerate stage title shuffling. Keep floors, rewards and reroll counts unchanged.
Equivalent seeded battles have the same winner and effects. Turbo changes presentation time, not floor progression or saved stats.
64 character ability descriptions are cataloged. Twelve have mechanics, including burn, revive, aura, time stop and multi-hit attacks.
Both teams can use implemented passives. Title feedback shows activation. Temporary buffs and effects do not overwrite baseStats.
Support BURN, CHILL, TAUNT, Soul Gem, Marine Solidarity and Witch behavior. Stand Arrow can grant implemented passives up to the cap.
Burn refreshes without stacking. Chill slows ATB. Taunt changes targeting. Unit abilities respect the cap and battle scope.
Store relics, equipment and consumables as item instances. Group them in Inventory and show descriptions.
The bag survives reload. Equipped icons appear on unit portraits. Used consumables are removed without a history log.
Nichirin Sword grants +15 ATK, Air Gear +15 SPD, and White Whistle buffs the strongest other ally by 5%. Cap equipment at three per unit.
Duplicate items stack. White Whistle cannot target its owner. BST ties pick the first eligible ally. Saved baseStats are unchanged.
Going Merry and Thousand Sunny each add one permanent slot during the run. Each relic is unique per player inventory.
Owned unique relics cannot recur in reward choices. Extra units can attack, use passives and be replaced. Reset removes the relics.
Sukuna’s Finger transforms a unit, Master Ball rolls an eligible UR, and Stand Arrow grants a passive or permanently empties a slot.
Actions validate the target and availability. Failure does not consume the item. Transformations roll fresh stats and discard replaced unit gear.
At each multiple of five cleared floors, offer three random eligible items and claim one.
A reward cannot be claimed twice. Progress waits for the outstanding reward. Bosses are not the sole reward trigger.
On upcoming floors 10,20,… show one boss pathway with no stage. Boss HP is 500 and ATK+DEF+SPD is 510 within UR bounds.
Bosses have red frames and BOSS tags. Loss leaves the boss encounter floor pending. Only one enemy unit is spawned.
Display Lure, Tailed Beast Bomb, Gun Fiend, Adaptation and Form Change. Bosses currently fight as stat-only units.
Catalog and UI clearly distinguish descriptive previews from active boss mechanics.
Roll a stage before choosing opponents. Effect and neutral groups each have 50% probability, evenly split within the group.
The selected stage persists for its encounter. Bosses have no stages. Neutral stages display No effect.
Implement Punk Hazard, Budokai, Dangai, Valley of the End, Colosseum, Hope’s Peak Academy and Itomori.
Burn/chill, duels, sweeps, strongest-unit selection, side swaps, execution and HP-percent impact follow their definitions. Original teams return after combat.
Each of three ordinary pathways independently has a 15% event chance. Events use dialogs and saved choice/target/reward states.
An event replaces a team option. Its result applies once. Pending choices restore on reload. Boss pathways stay boss-only.
A Small White Creature offers Yes/No. Yes grants a selected eligible unit +15% ATK/DEF/SPD and the Soul Gem transformation rule.
No existing Soul Gem unit is eligible again. On death the Witch gains its boost, attacks both teams and must be defeated for player victory.
Yes starts an idle battle against five sampled Marines with +5% stats. Victory grants one of five captives to replace a team slot.
No skips safely. Loss follows normal life rules. Victory reward is saved and applies only once. Marine ability holders use implemented passives.
Separate descriptions/configuration in abilities, items, events and stages JSON from TypeScript mechanics. Keep stable IDs in saves.
Catalog edits do not rename saved IDs. Adding text alone is never assumed to implement a new mechanic.
Save jobs, teams, items and encounters as server-side JSON. Browser storage remembers import identifiers. Production starts from host environment variables.
No production .env file is required. Server storage location is configurable. Cross-device account identity is not yet available.
Implement more listed character passives in small batches. Document unsupported mechanics explicitly.
Each implemented passive has a battle test, activation feedback and correct reset behavior. Catalog-only passives remain visibly identified.
Add relics, equipment and consumables with distinct tactical benefits.
New items have valid IDs, descriptions, acquisition rules and tested interactions. Unique, stackable and target rules are explicit.
Add beneficial, harmful and neutral events with readable consequences.
Each event has a complete flow, persisted state and one-time rewards or penalties. No event can strand the run.
Add new battle environments and alternate rules without changing the effect/neutral split unless approved.
Each stage has a complete description, deterministic test and clear victory rule. Both sides are affected according to the rule.
Tune proc rates, cooldowns, heal fractions, damage modifiers and revive frequency using simulations.
Seeded mixed-team benchmarks reveal outliers. Changes have recorded rationale and do not alter stored rolled baseStats.
Balance equipment, permanent modifiers, extra slots and consumable risk. Define modifier order.
Stacking, aura removal, transformations and replacement are covered. Each modifier type has a documented order and cap where needed.
Compare event skips, fights, trades and harmful outcomes against normal pathway rewards.
Skipping events cannot produce unlimited safe progression. Reward strength and penalty severity match their floor bands.
Tune durations and damage. Review extra-slot teams, Witches, revives and Taunt under alternate victory conditions.
Stage-specific win rates and duration distributions are reviewed. Disallowed interactions are explicit and tested.
Support named choices beyond Yes/No, including trades and branching outcomes.
Choices use stable IDs. Server validates options and eligibility. Branches survive reload and cannot apply rewards twice.
Add a small event state model supporting choice, input, target, challenge, battle and result steps.
Current two events still work. Each step defines allowed inputs, continuation and cancellation behavior. No arbitrary code is executed from JSON.
Support short typed answers with defined validation and retry rules.
Whitespace/case policy, accepted answers and maximum length are specified. Invalid answers show a clear result without losing the run.
Support numeric selections for trades, wagers and allocation events.
Minimum, maximum and step are enforced on the server. The player cannot spend more resources than owned.
Support multiple-choice quizzes and small puzzles with defined correct outcomes and failure rules.
Question/answer pools are versioned. Correct, incorrect, repeat and interrupted attempts are tested.
Offer in-game wagers with explicit costs, possible outcomes and probabilities. No real-money stakes are planned.
Odds and maximum loss are shown before confirming. Wagers resolve once server-side and cannot duplicate rewards on retry.
Track milestones such as first boss, floor reached, special wins and item/ability discoveries.
Achievements unlock once from valid server outcomes, persist separately from run resets, and display progress.
Periodically summon a substitute with Taunt that must be defeated before the boss.
Substitute lifecycle, summon cap, targeting and death behavior are tested. Summoning cannot create an endless encounter.
Add a telegraphed periodic all-enemy attack.
Cooldown and damage are configurable. All valid enemies are hit once per activation. Counterplay and feedback are visible.
Revive by taking a random player unit and using its battle stats plus a boost.
Define whether the chosen unit leaves battle. Transformation occurs once and original saved player units return afterward.
Become immune to an ability after experiencing it once in the battle.
Specify what counts as an ability and affected effect. First application works, later applications are blocked, and immunity resets.
Cycle through Attack, Defense and Speed formes with temporary bonuses.
Exactly one form is active. Bonuses replace prior-form bonuses and never change saved baseStats.
Scale boss battle stats with floor/level bands while preserving clear first-boss difficulty.
A documented curve, caps and seeded benchmarks exist for each band. Boss identity and stat changes are inspectable.
Select bosses from floor-band pools with configurable weights and repetition policy.
Every boss floor has an eligible pool. Weights and boundary floors are tested. No-stage and single-pathway rules remain intact.
Centralize floor-band rules for opponent size, eligible characters, passive guarantees, equipment and bosses.
One configuration governs generation. Every band has valid pools and deterministic boundary tests. Encounter policy is saved at creation.
Increase ordinary enemy team size at selected progression thresholds.
All teams fit the UI. Stages with five-slot rules retain explicit behavior. Empty/extra slots cannot silently change the winner.
Guarantee a configured number of enemies with implemented battle passives on later floors.
Count includes only functioning mechanics. Ineligible pools follow a documented fallback and never loop indefinitely.
Equip enemy units on later floors using allowed item pools and per-unit limits.
Generated gear affects combat and is readable before selection. Consumables are not treated as equipment. No player inventory is modified.
Use floor-band eligibility and weights for enemy unit appearances while retaining MAL-based starting teams.
Eligibility source, favorite ranges and ability requirements are defined. Small collections have a deterministic fallback.
Tune the combined floor curve, loss rate, rewards and boss spikes after the new encounter policy works.
Report median floor reached and encounter win rates for fixed seed sets. Unexpected spikes are corrected before adding more scaling.
Give each active timed passive an independent clock instead of relying on a single prioritized cooldown selector.
A unit with two timed granted abilities activates both. Time stop, death, revive and cooldown reset behavior is deterministic.
Run reproducible encounter batches and report duration, win rate, damage, healing, revives and dominant combinations.
Same seed/configuration repeats results. Reports show team composition and floor band. Existing mechanics have regression baselines.
Add account identity and durable storage for teams, achievements and run state across browsers.
Sign-in maps saves to the correct owner. Migration preserves existing data. Authorization prevents accessing another player’s saves.
Version save formats and migrate older teams/items/encounters as content evolves.
Old fixtures load safely. Removed content IDs have explicit handling. Failed migrations preserve the original save.
Verify production saves survive redeploys. Add backup/restore and stale save cleanup appropriate to the host.
Restart and redeploy retain a sample run. Restore is tested. Backup and retention policy is documented.
Validate JSON IDs, categories, pools and numeric ranges. Label listed-only passives in game. Move boss metadata to a catalog if useful.
Invalid catalogs fail validation with a precise message. UI distinguishes previews from active mechanics. Saves retain stable IDs.
Show temporary stats, status duration, current targets and cause of death/revival in an optional detailed log.
Base and effective stats are distinguishable. Players can inspect why a unit died without cluttering compact battle cards.
Exercise drag/drop alternatives, keyboard dialogs, portrait overlays, hidden-tab catch-up and reload during each run state.
Touch equipment selection works. Dialog focus is usable. Reload cannot lose rewards, charge lives twice or regenerate the selected pathway.
Track upstream errors, request latency and import completion. Keep retries bounded and explain stale/unavailable data.
Provider failures do not erase a saved team. Import status exposes actionable failures and does not stall indefinitely.
Update README and UI notes that still say passives are all previews, encounters reset on reload, or that MALchups only uses FIGHT.
Descriptions match implemented behavior and clearly name remaining limits.
Design character level growth separately from original rolled stats. Decide how rerolls and transformations inherit progress.
Growth has its own saved fields and calculations. Original baseStats remain intact. No level formulas are added before design approval.
Explore battling other users’ saved teams with fair snapshots and reproducible server results.
Ownership, match rules, versioning and fairness are designed before public matchmaking. No canonical power scaling is used for base stats.

values: Recommendations are proposals. Decide these before committing the related implementation or balancing work.
Choose floor bands, enemy size caps and boss scaling curves.
Keep first 10 floors as the baseline. Add bands only after simulation benchmarks.
No concrete thresholds or multipliers were requested.
Define summons, unit capture and adaptation semantics.
Battle-only changes should restore saved units and equipment afterward.
Clarify summon slots/caps, captured unit removal and immunity categories before implementation.
Define extra-unit behavior in duels and HP-percent stages.
Preserve Budokai first-five rule. Explicitly document which extra units contribute in every other stage.
Avoid enemy-size progression accidentally invalidating stage win conditions.
Should skipping a no-risk event advance the floor?
Review skip rewards and floor advancement before difficulty scaling.
Current No choices advance progress. This may offer safer routes than fighting.
Choose gambling resources and loss limits.
Use in-game resources only with explicit stake limits and displayed odds.
No currency or wager economy is currently defined.
Keep permanent achievements separate from inventory/lives reset.
Browser import IDs are not a cross-device account system.
Choose enemy pool source and small-pool fallback.
Start with imported pool plus a clearly labeled curated fallback when guarantees cannot be met.
Current ordinary opponents come only from the player’s imported pool.
Choose persistent hosting storage and identity architecture.
Verify current filesystem durability first. Introduce a database when identity or multiple server instances require it.
Static JSON catalogs do not require a database. Player saves need durable storage.
Decide when level growth and reroll inheritance belong in scope.
Postpone until floor difficulty and modifiers are stable.
Earlier design intentionally excluded leveling and stat growth.
Choose baseline battle-duration targets and Turbo release behavior.
Retain 20–40 simulated seconds as the initial ordinary-battle design target, subject to measurement.
This target is not a verified measured result. Turbo is a testing feature.
Specify draw/timeout progression and life rules.
Write one explicit policy for timeouts, simultaneous death and stage ties.
Current battles can draw at the 120-second simulation cap. Review all result paths before scaling.
Confirm suggested priorities, scope and ownership.
Use Foundations, Progression, Content, Later as ordering suggestions rather than fixed dates.
No deadlines, staffing, effort estimates or committed release dates were supplied.
